validated_statements.subject: US
validated_statements.source_text: In 2017, there were 1.2 million heart failure hospitalizations in the United States among 924 000 patients with heart failure.4 This represents a 26% increase in heart failure hospitalizations and number of patients hospitalized with heart failure. Although the absolute number of patients with heart failure has partly grown as a result of the increasing number of older adults, the incidence of heart failure has decreased.5 Among US Medicare beneficiaries, heart failure incidence declined from 36 cases per 1000 beneficiaries in 2011 to 27 cases per 1000 beneficiaries in 2014 and remained stable through 2016.5 Divergent trends in the incidence of heart failure have been observed for those with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (decreasing incidence) and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (increasing incidence).

validated_statements.subject: chest x-ray
validated_statements.source_text: The chest x-ray is a useful initial diagnostic test for the evaluation of patients presenting with signs and symptoms of heart failure because it assesses cardiomegaly, pulmonary venous congestion, and interstitial or alveolar edema and may reveal alternative causes, cardiopulmonary or otherwise, of the patient’s symptoms. Apart from congestion, other findings on chest x-ray are associated with heart failure only in the context of clinical presentation.

validated_statements.subject: oxygen uptake
validated_statements.source_text: It provides analysis of gas exchange and yields measures of oxygen uptake (oxygen consumption/oxygen uptake), carbon dioxide output, and ventilation. These measures can be integrated with standard exercise testing variables, such as heart rate, blood pressure, electrocardiographic findings, and symptoms to provide insights into the physiologic mechanisms underlying a patient’s dyspnea.

validated_statements.source_text: Because of these observations, angioedema was an exclusion criterion in the first large trial assessing angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor therapy in patients with hypertension35 and then in the large trial that showed clinical benefit of angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor therapy in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.1 The rates of angioedema were numerically higher in patients treated with angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor than in patients treated with angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors in PARADIGM-heart failure, although this difference did not reach significance.1 angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor therapy should not be administered in patients with a history of angioedema because of the concern that it will increase the risk of a recurrence of angioedema.

validated_statements.subject: death
validated_statements.source_text: Death from any cause was reduced from 29% with placebo to 27% in those treated with omega-3 PUFA.2 The outcome of death or admission to hospital for a cardiovascular event was also significantly reduced. The REDUCE-IT trial randomized patients with established CVD or diabetes with risk factors to 2 g of icosapent ethyl (a highly purified EPA) twice daily or placebo and showed a reduced risk for the composite of cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, coronary revascularization, or unstable angina.3 In reported studies, omega-3 PUFA therapy has been well tolerated.

validated_statements.source_text: In a registry study of hyponatremia in acute decompensated heart failure, fluid restriction only improved hyponatremia marginally.1 A registered dietitian-guided fluid and sodium restriction intervention improved New York Heart Association functional classification and leg edema in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction who were not in stage D heart failure,2 and fluid restriction improved quality of life in a pilot RCT of patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (New York Heart Association class I to IV).3 In a meta-analysis of RCTs on fluid restriction in heart failure in general, restricted fluid intake compared with free fluid consumption did not result in reduced hospitalization or mortality rates, changes in thirst, the duration of intravenous diuretic use, serum creatinine, or serum sodium levels.4 The validity of a previous trial supporting clinical benefits of fluid restriction in heart failure is in

validated_statements.source_text: Patients in the low-dose group were more likely to require a 50% increase in the dose at 48 hours than were those in the highdose group, and all treatment groups had higher doses of diuretics compared with baseline preadmission doses, underlining the necessity to intensify and individualize diuretic regimen.1 MRAs have mild diuretics properties and addition of MRAs can help with diuresis in addition to significant cardiovascular benefits in patients with heart failure. Addition of low-dose dopamine to diuretic therapy in the setting of reduced estimated glomerular filtration rate did not improve outcomes in a study that included patients with all EFs, but a subset analysis showed increased urine output and weight loss in patients with left ventricular ejection fraction <0. with significant interaction of effect with left ventricular ejection fraction.

validated_statements.subject: tachyphylaxis
validated_statements.source_text: However, tachyphylaxis may develop within 24 hours, and up to 20% of those with heart failure may develop resistance to even high doses. Because of sodium nitroprusside’s potential for producing marked hypotension, invasive hemodynamic blood pressure monitoring (eg, an arterial line) is typically required, and nitroprusside is usually used in the intensive care setting; longer infusions of the drug have been associated, albeit rarely, with thiocyanate and cyanide toxicity, particularly in the setting of renal insufficiency and significant hepatic disease.

validated_statements.subject: PAVE trial
validated_statements.source_text: Early studies with right ventricular pacing showed benefit. However, when right ventricular pacing was compared with cardiac resynchronization in more recent trials, especially in those with reduced LVEFs, cardiac resynchronization therapy generally produced more benefit than right ventricular pacing. The PAVE (Left Ventricular-Based Cardiac Stimulation post AV Nodal Ablation Evaluation) and the BLOCK-heart failure (Biventricular versus Right Ventricular Pacing in Patients with AV block) trials included patients with left ventricular ejection fraction >35%, with mean EF 46%22 in PAVE and 40% in BLOCK-heart failure (enrolled ≤50%).

validated_statements.subject: heart failure
validated_statements.object: a condition characterized by the heart's inability to pump enough blood to meet the body's needs
validated_statements.source_text: Among older adults, low income, social isolation, and lack of caregiver support increase heart failure mortality and low quality of life. Nursing home residents, and elderly inpatients with acute heart failure, are at risk of inadequate guideline-directed medical therapy prescription, although interventions in nursing facilities can improve care delivery for heart failure.–45 Lower socioeconomic status is associated with heart failure incidence and heart failure mortality. Homelessness,48 substance use, food insecurity, and lack of transportation each represent potential barriers to optimal disease management.49 Case management and social work services are essential to the comprehensive multidisciplinary heart failure team approach for coordinating complex medical, psychiatric, and social needs across multiple sectors.
